title: Add self-hosted runner(s) for tag/release platform jobs, gated so no self-hosted job can ever carry a pull_request trigger
description:
Split out of QCLI-326 (OPAG-166) as explicitly out of scope there: a security-posture change (attaching real hardware as a CI executor for a public repository) that this fleets own operating rules say cannot move on a peer relay of user approval alone. The user has since confirmed it directly in-session (2026-09-17), not just via opum-agents relay, and separately mentioned they also have a Linux VM and a Windows VM available in addition to the previously-discussed macOS arm64 machine (mini2). CPU architecture for the Windows/Linux VMs is not yet confirmed -- that determines which specific win32-*/linux-* legs each one can take over and is needed before finalizing scope here.

Cost context (OPAG-166): GitHub Actions macOS runners bill at roughly 10x Linux per minute and are the single biggest line item (38% of the fleets bill on 7% of the minutes); Windows is a smaller but real share (10%); Linux is already the cheapest per-minute runner and QCLI-326s trigger-scoping fix already eliminated most of quest-clis Linux run volume, so self-hosting Linux is lower priority and may not be worth the added attack surface.

The non-negotiable constraint, stated by opum-agent and independently agreed: GitHub self-hosted runners must never serve a public repository unless the trigger set structurally excludes pull_request -- a fork PR could otherwise execute arbitrary code on the users own machine. This only becomes safe here because QCLI-326 already scoped the jobs a self-hosted runner would take (immutable-candidates per platform target) to workflow_dispatch and tag pushes only, which a fork cannot trigger. Any workflow change adding a self-hosted runs-on label must be paired with a structural check (not a code-review convention) that fails CI if any self-hosted-labeled job is ever reachable from a pull_request trigger.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on which platform legs move to which self-hosted machine (macOS arm64 on mini2 at minimum; Windows and Linux legs assigned once VM CPU architecture is confirmed)
Each moved job targets workflow_dispatch or a tag push only, matching the condition immutable-candidates/candidate-bundle already use -- never pull_request, and never an ordinary branch push

A structural, automated check (not a comment or review convention) fails CI if any job carrying a self-hosted runs-on label is reachable from a pull_request trigger, proven by a deliberate violation going red and the real workflow staying green
Runner registration on each machine (mini2 at minimum) is completed and documented: how the runner is registered, kept online, and re-registered if the token expires
A tag/release run is exercised end to end against the self-hosted runner(s) and produces the same native-execution receipt shape as the GitHub-hosted run it replaces

plan: 1. Wait for winvm to be reachable (user runs vmctl start winvm from a GUI session on mbpm2, or opens screen sharing)
2. SSH into winvm (~/.scripts/winvm), install the GitHub Actions runner agent, register it against opum-ai/quest-cli scoped to win32-arm64 tag/release jobs only

3. Add a runs-on: [self-hosted, ...] leg gated to workflow_dispatch/tag-push (never pull_request), paired with a structural CI check that fails if any self-hosted-labeled job is ever reachable from pull_request
4. Confirm VM architecture/availability for the Linux VM and decide whether it is worth self-hosting given it is already the cheapest per-minute runner and QCLI-326 cut most of its volume
5. Exercise a real tag/workflow_dispatch run against the self-hosted runner(s) and confirm the native-execution receipt shape is unchanged
implementationNotes:
Additional cost context from opum-agent (OPAG-166), re-measured and worth carrying forward: the September billing split is macOS $106.08 (38%), Windows $27.61 (10%), Linux $146.38 (52%). Linux is the single biggest absolute line item despite being the cheapest per-minute runner -- it is high on volume, not price -- so it is a real lever here, just not the one the mini2 framing (macOS is overpriced per minute) was built around.

Explicitly flagged as UNMEASURED, not settled, by opum-agent: whether self-hosting Linux is actually cheaper once you count hardware, uptime and maintenance rather than only the GitHub Actions minutes it would zero out. Actions minutes go to zero; a VM does not maintain or power itself, and roughly 280 runs/day fleet-wide served by one or two always-on VMs is a different reliability/ops story than an elastic hosted pool. Whoever scopes the Linux leg of this task should measure that before treating self-hosted Linux as a given savings, not just port the macOS/Windows reasoning over unchanged.

Infrastructure identified directly by the user (2026-09-17): winvm is arm64 -- matches win32-arm64 exactly, the one leg that cannot be cross-compiled anywhere else, so it is the highest-value move. Access path: SSH launcher scripts already exist locally at ~/.scripts/mbpm2 (-> mbpm2.tail9905f8.ts.net, a Tailscale mesh address) and ~/.scripts/winvm (-> winvm.tail9905f8.ts.net directly, once the VM is up). mbpm2 is a physical Mac host running UTM guests (linuxvm, winvm, omarchy) controlled by ~/.scripts/vmctl.sh on mbpm2 itself (status/start/stop/restart), which shuts guests down gracefully from the inside rather than force-killing them (a 2026-08-02 force-kill corrupted linuxvms grub.cfg, which is why this script exists).

Read vmctl.sh before running anything (never executed blind). status/start/stop are safe, well-guarded operations -- start refuses if the VMs backing volume is not mounted, and stop tries a graceful in-guest shutdown before falling back to utmctl.

Current blocker: `vmctl status` on mbpm2 reports all three guests (linuxvm, winvm, omarchy) as "<not found - volume unmounted?>" -- their bundles live under /Volumes/VM/*.utm, and that path is not currently resolving on mbpm2. diskutil list on mbpm2 shows an internal APFS "VM" volume (81.3 GB, disk3s7) plus an unrelated external 4TB TimeMachineBackup volume, but nothing mounted at /Volumes/VM specifically at the time checked. Need to determine whether this is a volume that just needs mounting (diskutil mount) or something requiring physical/user action, before vmctl start winvm can work. Left uninvestigated further pending handoff -- do not guess at mounting the wrong volume on someone elses infrastructure.

Root cause of the unmounted-looking status found: it is not the volume or the script. /Volumes/VM is mounted (Windows.utm, Linux.utm present), UTM.app is running (confirmed pid via pgrep), and the user can see the VMs listed in UTMs own window. `utmctl list`/`utmctl status` over SSH fail with OSStatus -1743 ("not authorized to send Apple events") and utmctl itself prints "utmctl does not work from SSH sessions or before logging in." vmctl.sh mistakes that failure for "bundle not found" (its bundle_path() check calls utmctl status first and treats any failure the same way) -- a small diagnostic-message improvement worth making in vmctl.sh someday (distinguish "AppleEvents denied/SSH session" from "volume actually not mounted"), but not the blocker itself.

The actual blocker: Apple Events automation of a GUI app requires the caller to run inside the same logged-in GUI (Aqua) session as the target; SSH is never part of that session regardless of permissions granted. So `vmctl start winvm` cannot be run from this (or any) SSH session -- it needs to run from a GUI session on mbpm2 directly (physically at the machine, or via Screen Sharing/VNC/ARD into its console). Asked the user to either run it themselves or open a screen-sharing session. Once winvm is up, SSHing into winvm itself (~/.scripts/winvm, a direct Tailscale address) is unaffected by this -- only utmctl control of the VM from outside the GUI session is restricted, not general SSH to guests.

Everything established so far, for whoever briefs or resumes this: winvm is arm64 (matches win32-arm64 exactly, the one leg nothing else can cross-compile). Access is ~/.scripts/mbpm2 (SSH to mbpm2.tail9905f8.ts.net over Tailscale, physical Mac host running UTM) and ~/.scripts/winvm (direct SSH to winvm.tail9905f8.ts.net once the VM is up). VM control is ~/.scripts/vmctl.sh on mbpm2 (status/start/stop/restart of UTM guests linuxvm/winvm/omarchy) -- read before running, never blind. The blocker hit: vmctl/utmctl CANNOT be driven over SSH at all -- utmctl itself fails with OSStatus -1743 ("not authorized to send Apple events") and prints "utmctl does not work from SSH sessions or before logging in." This is a hard Apple Events/GUI-session constraint, not a bug in vmctl.sh and not a permissions grant that can be requested around -- confirmed directly (UTM.app running, /Volumes/VM mounted with Windows.utm/Linux.utm present, VMs visible in UTMs own window, yet utmctl list/status fail identically over SSH). Starting/stopping a guest therefore requires a real GUI session on mbpm2: physically at the console, or via Screen Sharing/VNC/Apple Remote Desktop into it. Plain SSH to the VM guests themselves (once started) is unaffected -- only utmctl control of UTM from outside the GUI session is restricted.

Also unresolved when reassigned: user has a Linux VM available too, architecture not yet confirmed; lower priority than winvm since Linux is already the cheapest per-minute GitHub-hosted runner and QCLI-326 already eliminated most of its wasted volume, so self-hosting it may not be worth the added public-repo attack surface -- worth a real measurement before assuming it saves money (opum-agent flagged the same caveat: Actions minutes go to zero, hardware/uptime/maintenance do not).

Non-negotiable constraint carried from OPAG-166 regardless of who executes: no self-hosted job may ever carry a pull_request trigger on this public repo, structurally enforced (a CI check, not a review convention), because a fork PR could otherwise execute arbitrary code on the users own machine.
